title: Lethe: Plasticity-aware Active Forgetting for Resource-Efficient On-Device Continual Learning

problem.claim: On-device continual learning must adapt to evolving task streams in dynamic edge environments while operating under limited model capacity on resource-constrained mobile devices.

gap.claim: Existing continual learning methods primarily optimize learning performance while neglecting the tension between accumulated knowledge and limited model capacity, hindering model evolution for new task learning.

contributions.claim: Lethe is a plasticity-aware active forgetting scheme for on-device continual learning that treats forgetting as a potential solution to model-capacity constraints.
Lethe uses forgetting-based plasticity injection with order-aware selective forgetting and neuro-inspired plasticity injection to accelerate convergence on new tasks.
Lethe uses cost-aware forgetting recovery with deposited model parameters and task-priority-based recovery control to reduce the cost of recovering forgotten knowledge and prevent frequent recovery.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive evaluations show Lethe consistently outperforms state-of-the-art solutions.
The authors report model-accuracy improvements of up to 8.93%.
The authors report an average reduction in computation overhead of 53.63%.

narrative_sequence.summary: On-device continual learning supports adaptation to evolving task streams in dynamic edge environments.
Existing methods neglect the tension between accumulated knowledge and limited capacity on resource-constrained mobile devices.
Lethe reframes forgetting as a potential solution and proposes plasticity-aware active forgetting.
The method combines plasticity injection for selective forgetting with cost-aware recovery for low-cost knowledge restoration.
The authors report accuracy gains and reduced computation overhead compared with state-of-the-art solutions.

source_observation.claim: Lethe applies order-aware selective forgetting and neuro-inspired plasticity injection to accelerate adaptation to new tasks.

interpretation.claim: Selective forgetting may improve adaptation when accumulated knowledge competes with limited model capacity.

application.claim: Resource-constrained continual learning systems could consider controlled, order-aware forgetting as an adaptation mechanism.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which task streams, forgetting policies, or deployment conditions determine when this approach is beneficial.

source_observation.claim: Lethe uses deposited model parameters and task priority to support cost-aware recovery of forgotten knowledge.

interpretation.claim: Maintaining recovery information can reduce the cost and frequency of relearning after forgetting.

application.claim: Continual learning systems could retain compact recovery information and prioritize recovery according to task importance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not quantify the storage cost or recovery trade-offs of deposited model parameters.

unknowns: Evaluation datasets, task streams, device configurations, and baselines are unspecified.
The abstract does not report experimental protocol details or variance across evaluations.
The storage overhead and recovery costs of deposited model parameters are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported improvements.
